summary: Weighted route refill drift causing opaque 429s on dedicated pool during background reweighting
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 429 responses for interactive chat calls routed through their Dedicated pool after we applied a route weight reallocation. The errors appear opaque (429 with minimal throttle headers) and affect a small subset of API keys for the account. Behavior began immediately after a background reweight job ran at 2026-03-12T02:00:00Z.

Impact:
- Customer's low-latency chat flow experiences ~5-10% request failures (429) for a 90-minute window during the reweighting activity.
- Customer is on a committed Dedicated pool and requires predictable throughput for business-critical chat sessions.

Environment:
- Deployment: Dedicated pool (tenant: triton-analytics-dedicated-01)
- Region: us-west-2
- Routes: chat-stream (priority class: low-latency), ingest-bulk (background warmup)

Expected behavior:
- Route weight changes should not cause opaque 429s; throttle headers should indicate remaining tokens and refill schedule.

Actual behavior:
- Intermittent 429 responses lacking consistent X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-Refill-Timestamp values.
- Errors correlate with background route weight shift and autoscaler warmup traffic spikes.

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Schedule a route weight reallocation that increases weight for background ingest route by 3x for 10 minutes.
2) Simultaneously run steady interactive chat traffic from 10 workers (session token reuse).
3) Observe occasional 429 responses on chat-stream requests during the weight change window.

Notes: customer provided a small client replay and traced timestamps (see logs).
steps_to_reproduce: Trigger a route weight reallocation that boosts background route weight for a short period
Maintain low-latency chat traffic concurrently from multiple worker processes
Monitor for 429s and inspect throttle response headers and console token-window graphs
logs_and_traces: Sentry: repeated 429 traces with parent request id and no throttle metadata; sample id: 9f2c4a
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: token refill orchestration lag between route-weight controller and rate-limiter leading to temporary misallocation of burst credits

Observed: dedicated-pool autoscaler issued warmup traffic on the background route during the same time window (confirmed in autoscaler logs). Warmup traffic appears to have been counted against tenant burst pool in addition to route-level bucket.
Rate-limiter code path review: there is a smoothing/refill pass that runs on a per-route schedule; route weight updates are applied asynchronously and may not be atomic with refill window alignment
Correlated metrics show token-window counter decrement on chat-stream while ingest route weight increased — suggests cross-route accounting when burst pools are shared
Throttle headers are missing when the gateway path returns an internal shortcut 429 path (we found a code path that returns early when shared-burst pool is marked exhausted)

Reproduction in staging: We reproduced a smaller-scale 429 surge when programmatically triggering a weight reallocation and simultaneously pushing background warmup traffic; headers were present there, pointing to partial metadata propagation in prod path (edge proxy to origin header rewrite suspected)
comments: Priya Patel (2026-03-12): Customer submitted client replay and timestamps. They've blocked a production deploy until we confirm root cause.
Liam Chen (2026-03-12): Assigned to SRE. First-pass inspection shows coincident warmup traffic from autoscaler. Will check token accounting and edge proxy header path.

Marta Gonzales (SRE) (2026-03-12): Confirmed autoscaler warmup events at 2026-03-12T02:00:45Z. Extracted ingress logs; found some requests returned by edge without throttle headers. Added a high-priority trace to follow header propagation.

Ethan Wright (Platform) (2026-03-13): Patch candidate prepared to add defensive header population on early-409/429 fast-path. Also toggling shared-burst isolation flag for the customer's pool to mitigate immediate impact.
Priya Patel (2026-03-13): Customer accepted temporary isolation toggle; reports drop in 429s. Requesting postmortem and permanent fix ETA.
resolution: Mitigated - temporarily enabled isolated burst pool for triton-analytics-dedicated-01 and scheduled a hotfix to ensure throttle headers are populated on early-exit 429 code paths and to align route-weight application with token refill windows.
follow_up_actions: Ship hotfix to edge-proxy to populate throttle headers on early 429 exit path (PR ready: edge-proxy/pull/241)
Deploy route-weight controller change to apply weight and trigger a refill alignment event atomically
Add an automated canary test that replays weight changes while generating mixed background and interactive traffic
Add dashboard panel showing per-route burst pool attribution during reweight events
Document recommended operator practice: perform weight reallocation with background route in paused warmup mode or staggered windows
customer_impact_summary: Customer experienced intermittent chat failures due to shared-burst accounting during a route reweight; tenant experienced increased 429s for ~90 minutes until isolation toggle applied.
